command:
export LBL=sizing THREADS=32
set -euo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp
LBL="${LBL:-unknown}"; THREADS="${THREADS:-16}"

CG=/sys/fs/cgroup
sample(){ : > /tmp/samp.tsv
  while :; do printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(date +%s)" \
    "$(cat $CG/memory.current 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" \
    "$(awk '/^usage_usec/{print $2}' $CG/cpu.stat 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" >> /tmp/samp.tsv
    sleep 1; done; }
sample & SP=$!; trap 'kill $SP 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT

echo "== unpack the full primary assembly + annotation (STAR needs them uncompressed) =="
gunzip -c GRCh38.primary_assembly.fa.gz > genome.fa
gunzip -c GRCh38.116.gtf.gz            > genes.gtf
printf 'genome_fa_bytes\t%s\ngtf_bytes\t%s\n' "$(wc -c < genome.fa)" "$(wc -c < genes.gtf)" | tee "size-$LBL.txt"

# Index and align in ONE task, deliberately: a full human STAR index is ~30 GiB, and moving
# that through S3 between two tasks would cost more than building it. One image, one tool.
echo "== STAR genomeGenerate: the WHOLE human genome =="
T0=$(date +%s)
STAR --runMode genomeGenerate --runThreadN "$THREADS" --genomeDir idx \
     --genomeFastaFiles genome.fa --sjdbGTFfile genes.gtf --sjdbOverhang 100 \
     --outFileNamePrefix gg_ > gg.log 2>&1 || { tail -25 gg.log Log.out 2>/dev/null; exit 1; }
T1=$(date +%s)
IDXB=$(du -sb idx | awk '{print $1}')

echo "== STAR align: the complete ERR188026 run =="
STAR --runThreadN "$THREADS" --genomeDir idx \
     --readFilesIn ERR188026_1.fastq.gz ERR188026_2.fastq.gz --readFilesCommand zcat \
     --outSAMtype BAM Unsorted --outFileNamePrefix al_ > al.log 2>&1 \
  || { tail -25 al.log al_Log.out 2>/dev/null; exit 1; }
T2=$(date +%s)
kill $SP 2>/dev/null || true

IN=$(awk -F'\t' '/input reads/{gsub(/[^0-9]/,"",$2); print $2}'        al_Log.final.out)
UNIQ=$(awk -F'\t' '/Uniquely mapped reads number/{gsub(/[^0-9]/,"",$2); print $2}' al_Log.final.out)
PCT=$(awk -F'\t' '/Uniquely mapped reads %/{gsub(/[^0-9.]/,"",$2); print $2}'      al_Log.final.out)
BAM=$(wc -c < al_Aligned.out.bam)
PEAK=$(awk -F'\t' '{if($2+0>m)m=$2+0} END{printf "%.2f", m/1073741824}' /tmp/samp.tsv)
CORES=$(awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{u=$3;t=$1} END{printf "%.2f", ($3-u)/1e6/($1-t)}' /tmp/samp.tsv)
{
printf 'label\t%s\n' "$LBL"
printf 'star_version\t%s\n' "$(STAR --version)"
printf 'threads\t%s\n' "$THREADS"
printf 'index_wall_s\t%s\n' "$(( T1 - T0 ))"
printf 'index_bytes\t%s\n' "$IDXB"
printf 'align_wall_s\t%s\n' "$(( T2 - T1 ))"
printf 'total_wall_s\t%s\n' "$(( T2 - T0 ))"
printf 'input_reads\t%s\n' "$IN"
printf 'uniquely_mapped\t%s\n' "$UNIQ"
printf 'pct_unique\t%s   (assert >= 85)\n' "$PCT"
printf 'bam_bytes\t%s\n' "$BAM"
printf 'peak_rss_gib\t%s\n' "$PEAK"
printf 'avg_cores\t%s\n' "$CORES"
} | tee -a "size-$LBL.txt"
test "$IN" -gt 5000000 || { echo "only $IN reads -- not a full run"; exit 1; }
awk -v p="$PCT" 'BEGIN{ if (p+0 < 85) { printf "only %s%% uniquely mapped\n", p; exit 1 } }'
test "$BAM" -gt 500000000 || { echo "BAM is only $BAM bytes"; exit 1; }
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
